variation_result: Eight new tiles baked through the same generator (sampler.py, jitter sizes taken from how much nine 418-dot windows of the reference differ from each other: stone share 4.5 %, big-stone share 7.4 %, soil crumbs 13.8 %). Same-kind score (texture_compare): 0.365-0.456 as baked (mean 0.403), 0.425-0.488 with the smoothed-height view (mean 0.457); the fitted tile S_v4 scores 0.362 / 0.435, so the new tiles are as good as the fitted one. Dot for dot against the reference they are poor, as wanted: SSIM 0.206-0.224, Delta E 20.5-21.4, edge skill 0.00-0.015, tier none. Against each other: mean dot difference 34.6 of 255, pair SSIM 0.19 (max 0.206), so they are not copies. All 8 seamless (seam ratio 0.97-1.08). Contact sheet: variations/contact_sheet.png; numbers: variations/report.json. Looking at the sheet: they read as gravel on rusty soil, but stones are more kite-shaped and smooth than the reference's chunky chipped blocks and the soil is flatter and darker.
area_result: One 2508 x 2508 picture (a 2 x 2 tile area of NEW content, 4 times the stones and soil lumps from one description, area/descriptions/sample_101.json, 2.5 KB) baked in 173 s on the shared machine. Seam jump at the middle lines and at the wrap edge compared with normal dot-to-dot jumps: 1.06 / 1.10 (middle, vertical / horizontal) and 0.95 / 1.05 (wrap edge); about 1.0 = no seam (the reference tile itself has 2.5). The four 1254 quadrants differ from each other: pair SSIM 0.17-0.18, best shifted correlation 0.039 (a repeat would give 1.0). Preview: area/area_preview_1254.png, numbers: area/area_report.json. Also the half-tile-shift test on the 1254 tile: mean colour difference 1.29 of 255, 0 % of dots over 40 (a wrong roll gives 31 and 28 %): seamless.
resolution_result: Same description (S_v4) baked at 512 / 1254 / 2508 dots: 19 s / 100 s / 173 s (shared machine, upper bounds; colour render 3 / 29 / 64 s, height render 3 / 31 / 52 s, python shape list + mesh 9 / 23 / 9 s, file sets 2.3 / 11.5 / 38.7 MB). The picture is the same: after shrinking both to 512 the 1254 and 2508 bakes match the 512 one with SSIM 0.99 and 1.7 levels mean difference. What changes: edges get sharper (change between neighbouring dots per tile dot 4.3 / 5.7 / 6.5) and the height blur and normal strength are scaled by dots per pixel so the normal map keeps its slope (mean slope 0.374 / 0.367 / 0.352). Crops: guide_pictures/resolution_crops.png.
transfer_result: New surface: ROUNDED PEBBLES ON SAND, made from S_v4 by changing numbers only (21 description keys: 8 pebble tones, 8 sand tones, 7-12 corners per stone and almost no chipping, softer shadow, fewer bigger pebbles with looser packing, no extra facets, light from the top left, fewer sand lumps) plus ONE number found again: the height stretch (the gravel stretch would have turned the bright sand all white; fixed by stretching the tile's own 1st and 99th percentile to 10 and 245). No generator code was touched. About 12 minutes of my work (one 70-line script, one import slip), 1.9 KB description, bake 48 s. Looks like a pebble beach (transfer/pebbles_sheet.png), half-tile seamless test passed (colour difference 1.54, 0 % over 40). Changes list: transfer/pebbles_changes.json, report: transfer/transfer_report.json. No reference exists for pebbles, so there is no score to quote; judged by eye.
geometry_route_verdict: Tried a real-geometry route on the same stone list: a Geometry Nodes group (one point per stone, Instance on Points of a 4-, 5- or 6-sided short column with a shrunk top, turned and sized from point attributes, Realize Instances, Set Material), photographed from above. It builds and photographs in about 9 s at 1254 (2832 stones) against 65-100 s for the flat painter, and the true height/normal look good (guide_pictures/geometry_route_compare.png). But scored against this reference, whose maps come from the colour, it is WORSE on same-kind: geometry alone 0.173; painter colour with geometry height 0.203; 50/50 hybrid 0.257; painter alone 0.362 (smoothed-height view 0.435 / 0.247 / 0.435). Normal angle error is lower for geometry (28.5 / 29.0 / hybrid 33.0 against painter 37.8) but only because smooth normals sit closer to the flat-normal level (24.5), not because the structure matches. Verdict: use geometry for real 3D displacement of a gravel floor, not to reproduce these colour-derived maps. The research hint that 50/50 hybrids help gravel did NOT hold here.
derivation_ceiling: Height = clip((267.15 x R + 91.48 x G + 210.5 x B)/255 - 17.7, 0, 255) of the colour (sRGB 0-255) after a 0.5-dot blur: mean error 5.02 steps of 255 against the uploaded 8-bit height (correlation 0.994; a free 64-point curve gives the same 5.0; the usual 0.299/0.587/0.114 grey does worse, green hardly counts). Normal = slope of the 8-bit height x strength: from the UPLOADED height, central differences strength 10 gives 0.34 degrees; from the height made from the reference colour, 5.9 degrees (central, 12) or 4.6 degrees (Sobel, 12); a flat normal is 24.5 degrees off. So the tier 'exact' normal limit (4 degrees) cannot be reached by any colour-derived description. Palette ceiling: snapping every dot to 24 colours gives Delta E 2.81, SSIM 0.923, edge skill 0.857, height error 8.1, normal 10.6 degrees (9.1 with Sobel), tier close; with a 3x3 majority filter SSIM 0.857, normal 13.4, tier layout. 8 colours: 4.43 / 0.855; 16: 3.32 / 0.902; 48: 2.15 / 0.954.
what_each_layer_bought: PROCEDURAL ladder (S_v4, scored with plain OpenCV drawings, same-kind score; bytes of the description): ground colour only 178 B (same-kind not defined, dot SSIM 0.44: a flat picture beats any invented texture on SSIM) -> + soil lumps 910 B: same-kind 0.197 -> + tiny soil specks 1.1 KB: 0.170 -> + tiny and small stones 1.9 KB: 0.247 -> + medium stones 2.0 KB: 0.345 -> + large stones 2.2 KB: 0.408 -> all five stone classes with shadow, rim, extra facets and flaky patches 2.4 KB: 0.437 (without shadow/rim/facets/patches the same stones score 0.352: that detail layer is worth +0.09). Baked in Blender: 0.362 as baked, 0.435 smoothed-height view.

Dot-for-dot SSIM FALLS as invented stones are added (0.44 flat ground -> 0.21): invented texture is uncorrelated with the reference, so SSIM must not be used on invented content; use the same-kind score and your eyes.

TRACED ladder (24-colour palette, patches written as first corner + small steps): patches over 600 dots + stamps over 120 = 49 KB, SSIM 0.43, edge skill 0.09 (the layout of the biggest stone masses only); patches over 250 = 85 KB, SSIM 0.45; over 100 = 204 KB, SSIM 0.51, edge 0.24; over 50 = 350 KB, SSIM 0.58, edge 0.41, tier layout.

STAMPS are the big win for a busy picture: the specks too small to outline are added back as three numbers each (x, y, radius under their colour, found as the dots where the drawn patches still disagree with the palette picture). Patches over 250 + 18 000 stamps (270 KB): SSIM 0.588, edge skill 0.593 (patches over 250 alone, 85 KB: 0.453, 0.114). Patches over 100 + 23 000 stamps (426 KB): SSIM 0.666, Delta E 5.3, edge 0.694, height error 18.5, tier layout. About +0.15 SSIM and +0.35 edge skill for +50 % bytes, against +0.07 SSIM for doubling the patch outlines.

What traced descriptions still miss: the normal error stays 22-25 degrees (limit for close is 12): the normal is the slope of the fine detail, and tiny edges must be placed to within a dot. Close needs ~all dots.
lessons_that_transfer: HOW TO START A NEW SURFACE (checklist in order). 1 Prove the derivation first (10 minutes, plain Python): fit a straight mix of red/green/blue with cut-offs + a small blur + a normal strength that turn the reference colour into the reference height and normal; the fit tells you the ceiling (gravel: height 5 steps, normal 4.6 degrees) and takes height and normal off your list. 2 Snap the colour picture to k colours and measure the ceiling of 'flat patches' (gravel needs 24 colours for tier close; 8 colours already SSIM 0.855). 3 COUNT the patches (gravel 226 000 raw at 24 colours) before choosing a description style: a busy picture cannot be traced into 512 KB; slate could. 4 Measure statistics instead of hunting for individual elements when the elements touch: share of each class, the size curve ('survives opening with growing discs'), colour mix per size, shadow band width, light direction, how much windows of the picture differ. 5 Build the generator as a painter: flat polygons drawn back to front (soil lumps big first with small on top, stones small to big, each stone = shadow under, rim, body, lit face, shaded face, flaky patches), each drawn again one tile over where it crosses an edge; Blender photographs them from above with Emission materials; then derive height and normal from the colour with the proven rule. 6 Calibrate counts and spacing automatically against the measured size curve (coordinate search with a plain OpenCV drawing, no Blender: about 4 s per try), then check sizes BY EYE against the biggest elements: my first calibrated version matched the mask curve but had stones 1.5 x too small. 7 Score with both tools and look at every sheet. 8 Only then write the sampler, the variations, the area, the resolutions, the transfer.

The height stretch is the one number that must be found again for every new surface (gravel's stretch turns bright sand white); take the tile's own 1st and 99th percentile of the mix and stretch them to 10 and 245.
Stamps (tiny round patches = 3 numbers) beat outlines for the many small specks of a busy picture; find them as the residual between the drawn patches and the palette picture.

Soil darker next to stones is a shadow band (24.6 vs 31.4 lightness over 8 dots), not a dark outline; light came from the top (lightness rises 0.061 per dot going up): measure both before choosing the stone shading.
Painter order matters: shadows and rims under each stone, small stones first, big on top; soil lumps big first, small on top (my first soil drew big lumps last and hid all the grain).

Do not use dot-for-dot SSIM on invented content (a flat picture beats it); do not use the same-kind score alone either (it did not see the blocky shapes or hue errors my eyes saw). Seed noise in the same-kind score is 0.03-0.05 here.
Brightness-only jitter keeps the hue: independent jitter on red, green, blue turned dark grey stones purple and green.

Specific to gravel: stone size classes, stone chunkiness (3 corners = shards, 4 = blocks, 7-10 = pebbles), packing spacing, shadow width. General: derivation proof, palette ceiling, statistics + calibration, painter order, stamps, height stretch, wrap copies, half-tile test, two comparison tools. A new stone-like surface (pebbles on sand) needed numbers only plus the height stretch.
Real geometry (Geometry Nodes instances) is quick (9 s) and gives a true height, but for references whose maps were made from the colour it lowers the same-kind score; keep it for genuine 3D floors.
known_gaps: No description reaches tier 'close': best is 'layout' (426 KB: SSIM 0.666, Delta E 5.3, edge 0.694, height 18.5 all pass the close limits; only the normal error 22.3 degrees fails, limit 12). 'Exact' is impossible by the derivation ceiling (normal 4.6 > 4).

No class M description is good: traced M (49 KB) is tier none (SSIM 0.43); the layered idea 'place the big stones individually, invent the rest' was NOT built because I could not find individual stones (colour segmentation + watershed gave 237-364 clusters for about 1500 stones; a second try with biggest-inscribed-disc peaks gave the same under-split clusters and was deleted).

The procedural stones are still smooth kite-like polygons with a cartoon shadow; the reference stones are chunky chipped blocks with several faces, the soil is a grainy orange speckle and the biggest stones (110-160 dots long) are rarer and bigger. Mean Lab of a tile (S_v2 preview) 23.6, 3.8, 5.8 against reference 24.5, 2.5, 3.8: slightly too orange.
Same-kind scores of procedural tiles are 0.36-0.46: weakest groups are colour spectrum (0.11), colour scale (0.16), colour gradient (0.22); not chased further.

The procedural normal map is 37.8 degrees off the reference (worse than a flat normal, 24.5) because random micro-detail is uncorrelated; a lower strength or more blur would help the dot score but was not made a setting.
Roughness and metallic maps are a documented choice (no reference): soil 0.95, stones 0.55 to 0.8 by brightness, metallic 0. AO is a cheap cavity map from the height.

The three plain-language files (04 Recipe - gravel, 04 Lessons - gravel, analysis_findings.md) were NOT written because the harness refused to write .md report files; their content is in this answer (and the script headers explain each step).
Resolution/bake times are from a shared machine (load average 8-12 on 4 cores), so upper bounds. The sweep strips label 'used' values from S_v2 (shadow 6, chip 0.12) while S_v4 uses chip 0.1.
Mistake: one 'pkill -f run_everything.sh' by name may have stopped another builder's script of the same name; the others should check their runs.
Disk: scratch pictures, 7 of 8 early texture sheets and extra map files of non-final bakes were deleted to get from 1.1 GB to 334 MB; the numbers of the deleted items are kept in scores/*.json.
dead_ends: Finding individual stones by colour (soil vs stone) plus a watershed: 237-364 under-split clusters for about 1500 stones (dark stones touch dark stones, shadows are stone-coloured, rusty stones are soil-coloured); replaced by statistics (size curve, colour mix, packing) and calibration.
Inscribed-disc peaks as stone centres for a 'placed stones' (class M procedural) description: the same under-split clusters (median radius 34 dots); abandoned and deleted.

Hybrid 'trace only the stone-coloured patches, make the soil procedurally' (TS_k24_a300, 54 KB): the small-patch clean-up pushed dark soil into the stones (stone share 0.83 against 0.68), SSIM 0.38, same-kind 0.215.
Tracing coarse patches only (over 600 / 250 dots): looks like stained glass and loses all the soil grain (SSIM 0.43-0.45, edge skill 0.09-0.11).
Calibrating stone counts against the size curve of a colour mask alone: it matched the mask but gave stones 1.5 x too small to the eye (S_v2, redone as S_v4 with sizes measured from the big stones).
Tone jitter and slightly lighter palettes: same-kind score moved only 0.01-0.02 (noise level); only the picture could choose.
Real-geometry hybrid height for gravel: lowers the same-kind score (0.257 against 0.362 for the painter alone).
Mode filter / smoothing the normal strength and blur on a traced colour gives only about 3 degrees (24.8 -> 21.8) on the normal error; the 12 degree limit is out of reach below near-total tracing.
Per-channel random colour jitter: made purple and green stones (fixed with brightness-only jitter, set 'jitter_mode': 'brightness').
changes_wanted_in_lib: pixel_compare.py: show the per-surface ceiling next to the tier limits (gravel: normal error 4.6 degrees even for a perfect colour, so 'exact' can never be reached; palette-snapped 24 colours gives 10.6 degrees so 'close' needs ~all dots). The normal limits should be derived from the derivation fit per surface.

pixel_compare.py / texture_compare.py: add a flag that says 'invented content' and skips dot-for-dot SSIM (a flat picture scores 0.44, any invented gravel 0.21); also offer the smoothed height (0.8 dots) as an option so score_folder does not need to make a texture_view copy.

description_audit.py: accept rows of equal length instead of calling a long first row a picture (stamps grouped per colour reach 3450 numbers per list and pass only because they stay under 4000); also report the size of the biggest list in the summary line.

Add a shared 'painter' tool to lib (polygon list -> real flat Blender geometry -> overhead Emission photographs -> height/normal derivation), the slate and gravel recipes now carry two copies of the same 150 lines; include the Cycles Gaussian-filter-width table (width 2 = 0.5 dot blur).

bake_harness.py: a helper that saves a loaded PNG back with the same encoding (load_png_as_array + save_array_png round trip works but is undocumented), and a way to crop at render time; sweep_tools.py renders the whole tile at small size, which makes sweeps of small features unreadable (my sweeps render at 640 and keep a 320 crop).
Add a tiny least-squares fitter (no scipy here): I wrote a 30-line Levenberg-Marquardt in analysis/derivation_parametric.py that others could reuse.
blender_tools_used: Mesh from points (mesh.from_pydata) + face attributes: every polygon of the painter list becomes one flat face with its own colour, height, roughness and metallic number
Attribute node + Emission shader: one material per picture shows exactly one channel (colour, height, roughness, metallic) with no lighting
Orthographic camera over a 1 x 1 square + Cycles with box pixel filter (colour, 16 samples) or Gaussian pixel filter width 4 x blur (height blur 0.5 dot)
Standard view transform for colour, Raw for data pictures, 16-bit PNG for height
Map-free height rule and normal derivation in numpy (central difference or Sobel, strength 10-12, scaled by dots per pixel for other sizes)
Tileable 4D donut noise group (lib recipe_tools) offered for an optional height grain (not used in the final descriptions)

Geometry Nodes: Mesh Cylinder, Input Normal + Dot Product + Greater Than, Scale Elements (shrunk tops), Transform, Geometry to Instance, Join Geometry, Named Attribute, Combine XYZ, Instance on Points (Pick Instance), Realize Instances, Set Material; geometry modifier on a point cloud object (gn_tools GeoWriter, photograph_geometry)
Wrap copies (nine copies of every shape that touches the tile edge) for seamlessness, checked with the half-tile-shift test
Blender command line: blender -b --disable-autoexec -t 2 --python generator/gravel_generator.py -- DESCRIPTION OUT --size N, with --batch jobs files and --shift 0.5 0.5
Not used: shader-node procedural noise/Voronoi recipes (the research route G4), rigid-body physics, curves, compositor
